html:
The Waíkhana, known in Spanish and Portuguese as Piratapuyo, are an Indigenous people of the Papurí and Vaupés rivers on the border of Colombia and Brazil. They speak a language of the Eastern Tucanoan family.

The Vaupés is known for linguistic exogamy: people must marry someone from another language group, so a typical household speaks several languages. The Waíkhana take part in this system with neighbours such as the Pisamira and the Tucano. They live in riverside villages, fishing and growing bitter manioc. Catholic missions and the rubber trade reshaped the region in the 1900s.
